note: A small site (45 by 35 ft, full sun on the booking page) up a dirt driveway of about 260 ft on the west side of Montour Road, 7.6 miles from PA 120. The driveway rises 5 to 7 m from the road, about 7 to 8% on dirt, so it is for dry weather. The agency's campsite map layer marks the site as having no trailer access, while the booking page sells it as an RV and trailer site. Montour Road from PA 120 is a severe climb: about 10% held for 2.6 miles (411 m of rise). The gentler way is from PA 872 by Elk Lick Run Road and Trout Run Road, whose one hard pitch is about 10.5% for 0.8 mile, followed by 10 miles of ridge road. All of it is dirt or gravel forest road. No toilet. Pack out trash. --Claude
summary: Site page re-read: 060 Bronson still listed and bookable online, Drive-In, RV/Tent/Trailer categories, 25 ft, clearance 20 ft, dirt pull-in driveway 260 ft (no grade listed; 3DEP 7-8%). Access road is the finding: the stated approach is ~10% for 4.2 km, far longer than the Spade Road yardstick; the northern approach is about at the yardstick. Reported as a drop candidate. Fees confirmed, $6.50 fee added; season written; facilities none. Imagery is cloud-covered at the pin (a pale strip about 20 m west may be the opening): pad not confirmed, pin not moved. NHD: nothing within 200 m.
flags: DROP CANDIDATE (ruling 9, access road much longer than the yardstick): Montour Road from PA 120 (the page's own route) climbs 411 m in one unbroken 4.2-km run at a 9.7-9.8% mean (steepest 200 m 11.7-11.9%): the same grade as Spade Road but three and a half times as long. From the north, PA 872 > Elk Lick Run Road 3.8 mi > Trout Run Road 1.5 mi > Montour Road, the one hard climb is 10.5% for 1.35 km on Elk Lick Run Road with the steepest 200 m at 14.3%: about the Spade Road yardstick itself. A third way, Swank Road from First Fork Road, runs 9.1% for 1.15 km then 8.9% for 1.9 km. Surfaces not confirmed (page: 'state forest dirt or gravel roads'). For this site the northern approach also adds 10.75 mi of Montour Road with a 900-m descent at 8.9% and a 650-m rise at 7.7%. On top of that the driveway is DIRT, 260 ft, with no grade on the page: 3DEP has the road 5.3 m below the pin at 57 m and 6.7 m below at 84 m, about 7-8% mean, 14% over the steepest ~30 m of the straight line (10-m DEM). Site is 45 x 35 ft with a 25-ft limit. Left in place with both approaches and the driveway in the note; single-site entry, so taking it out is a drop.

DCNR GIS layer vs booking page (ruling 5, kept, both in the note): the GIS record for this site says TrailerAccess 'No'; the booking page lists 'Looking For Category: RV Site, Tent Site, Trailer Site' and a 25-ft maximum vehicle length.
Imagery: the Esri tile at the pin is under cloud; the pad and driveway could not be seen and the pin position on the pad is unconfirmed (RA point and GIS point agree).

Season written (entry had none): opens 04-01, closes 12-12, from the site page's own statement ('open from the beginning of April through the end of rifle deer season') and 'Status: Open through Sat Dec 12 2026'. The engine's calendar is a little wider at the front: it shows nights Available from early March 2027 (Not Available through 5 March, Available on 11 March; 6-10 March not probed). I wrote the agency's stated April opening; a March night the engine sells is outside the stated season.
